steps.text: Take Prednisone 40 mg once a day for 2 more days (next 2 days)
Take Doxycycline 100 mg twice a day for 3 more days (next 3 days)
Take Furosemide 40 mg once a day (the new, higher dose)
Use your maintenance inhaler every day; use the rescue inhaler only when breathing gets hard
Weigh yourself every day and write it down
Use your home oxygen at the flow rate and times you were prescribed
Stop smoking. Ask your care team for help and resources
See your primary care doctor (as arranged)

medications.name: Prednisone
medications.howOften: once a day by mouth for 2 more days
medications.why: A steroid pill that calms the swelling in your lungs. Take both remaining days.

medications.name: Doxycycline
medications.howOften: twice a day by mouth for 3 more days
medications.why: An antibiotic to finish treating the pneumonia. Take every dose.

medications.name: Furosemide
medications.why: Your water pill at a higher dose than before. It takes extra fluid off so you breathe easier. You will urinate more.

medications.name: Maintenance inhaler
medications.why: Keeps your airways open. Use it every day even when you feel fine.

medications.name: Rescue albuterol inhaler
medications.howOften: as needed when breathing gets hard
medications.why: Opens your airways fast during a bad spell.

medications.name: Carvedilol
medications.howOften: at the dose on your discharge list
medications.why: Helps your heart and blood pressure.

medications.name: Previous lower-dose furosemide regimen
medications.why: Stopped. The new 40 mg dose replaces it. Do not take both.

medications.name: Any duplicate inhaler therapy
medications.why: Stopped. Use only the inhalers on your final medication list so you do not double up.

followUps.why: Check your recovery and your medicines
Check your COPD plan, inhalers and oxygen
Check your heart failure and the furosemide dose

warnings.text: Severe shortness of breath that your rescue inhaler does not help
Blue or gray lips, or you cannot speak because you are so breathless
New confusion or you cannot stay awake
You need much more oxygen than usual
High fever or a cough that quickly gets worse with more phlegm
Fast weight gain with more swelling or trouble breathing when lying flat
You are using the rescue inhaler more than usual
You are not sure which inhaler to use or how to use it
